hints: Search: 'elephant trumpet', 'elephant trumpeting close', 'african elephant trumpet call', 'asian elephant trumpet' (freesound CC0/CC-BY, Wikimedia Commons, Pixabay). Ideal segment: one loud, brassy, raspy trumpet blast ('praaah') with rich noisy harmonics reaching 5 kHz and above and an abrupt onset, 0.6-1.2 s (minimum 0.5 s). Pitfalls: not a clean single-tone whine or howl (a pure harmonic tone around 750 Hz is heard as a dog); no zoo crowd voices, music or hall reverb. Do not reuse ikbenraar freesound 819668 (the source of this dog-like clip), and use a different original than sprint_1 (Wikimedia Elephant_voice_-_trumpeting.ogg). Audit gate: Dog/Howl/Bark must not appear.

replace.name: 개 무리 공용

hints: Search: 'large dog panting', 'big dog panting heavy', 'husky panting', 'german shepherd panting'. This file is the fallback tired sound for wolf and sleddog, so it must be a big dog. Ideal: 1.5-2.5 s steady rhythmic panting, 3-5 breaths/s, low voiced 'hah' with energy mostly under 2 kHz, dry, no licking, collar jingle or hum. replace.name: 집고양이
why: cat_tired_1.mp3: 사람 틀리다, 후보 없음: 지워 (앱에서 뺐다)
hints: Search: 'cat panting', 'cat breathing fast', 'cat open mouth breathing', 'cat heavy breathing' (freesound CC0/CC-BY, Pixabay). Ideal: real domestic cat, unvoiced fast airy breaths (3-6 per second) whose breath noise reaches 3-8 kHz, no pitched voice, close mic, dry room, 0.8-2.5 s continuous. Pitfalls: human imitating a cat (voiced 'huh huh' at 150-250 Hz with nothing above 2 kHz, which is the current problem), dog panting (tongue slap, bigger and lower), purring (steady 25 Hz rumble is not panting), room reverb. If no clean real cat panting exists, delete the file and let the fallback/synth play (README allows leaving it empty).
